The offline Python consumers use a credential-free Linux local-job runtime. The shared action reads two repository variables: `DOCSPEC_LOCAL_RUNTIME_URL` (public HTTPS tar.gz) and `DOCSPEC_LOCAL_RUNTIME_SHA256` (the approved archive digest). It never reads a secret or the remote/lake runtime configuration.

The owner must supply and qualify the real Linux artifact. Its four regular root files are `docspec` (executable), `runtime.json`, `limits.json`, and `build.json`. `build.json` contains exactly `version: 1`, `source_revision`, `platform: "linux-amd64"`, `build_features` (ordinary `remote`, without `test-util`), and `binary_sha256`. The runtime repeats those pins and names `./docspec`, `./limits.json`, and `./workspace`. The six positive integer limits are the owner's Linux limits; installation preserves them exactly.

The installer checks archive bytes before extraction, stages regular files privately, checks metadata and binary identity, runs `scripts/dev.py doctor --lane production-offline`, and only then exports `DOCSPEC_JOB_CONFIG`. A malformed artifact, missing approval, stale destination, or failed doctor stops the job before capture credentials or offline consumers. Local packaging tests use an authored ELF-shaped fixture; they do not prove Linux engine execution or qualify resource limits.

Owner preparation: build the ordinary Linux engine in the engine-owned worktree, package the four approved files, qualify the selected limits on Linux, and set the two variables. This agent did not upload an artifact, wire variables, dispatch a workflow, or access credentials.
